$comment: What a lab does through the VS Code panels, as answer rules, so a machine can walk it.
Read by the lab driver of the extension (vscode-sfdx-hardis, yarn test:ui:labs), which opens
a real Extension Development Host on a learner's clone and drives the real panels against the
real Salesforce CLI and the real orgs. The same rule shape is understood by the headless
harness of the training-e2e skill, so a lab's answers are written once and can be replayed at
A rule fires once, in the order it appears here:
{ q: regex on the question, choice: regex on a choice title }
{ q: ..., value: text typed in the box }
{ q: ..., value: '__INITIAL__' }        accepts what the panel pre-fills
{ q: ..., choice: ..., optional: true } may not be asked
A question no rule covers FAILS the lab on purpose: a learner reading the lab would be stuck
on that same question, so either the lab forgot to mention it or the command should not ask it.
A lab with a 'skip' is one the driver cannot walk, and the reason is what the run reports as
not covered. Keep it honest: the labs that end in a browser or on GitHub are not panels.
A choice regex must not be anchored with ^: the panel prefixes most choice titles with an
emoji, so an anchored "Scratch org" never matches the row the learner clicks. Match the words.
When a lab's questions change, this file changes with the lab text, in the same Pull Request.
